title: High-field fate of the Kitaev quantum spin liquid in $α$-RuCl$_3$
authors: K. Imamura, R. Ohno, Y. C. Tsuzuki, Y. Akui, R. Namba, K. Ishihara, M. Akaki, M. Kimata, N. Kurita, H. Tanaka, N. Kimura, S. Imajo, A. Matsuo, K. Kindo, Y. Matsuda, K. Hashimoto, Y. Mizukami, T. Shibauchi
abstract: Kitaev quantum spin liquids (KQSLs) host fractionalized excitations described by itinerant Majorana quasiparticles and gapped $Z_2$ fluxes (visons), providing a platform for emergent topological matter. Whether such a state survives under strong magnetic fields, however, remains an open question. The layered honeycomb magnet $α$-RuCl$_3$ is a leading candidate material: an in-plane field of $\sim$ 7 T suppresses antiferromagnetic order and induces a quantum-disordered phase exhibiting signatures consistent with Majorana excitations, including an anomalous thermal Hall effect and field-angle-dependent specific heat. At higher fields, the magnetization approaches saturation, suggesting a transition to a spin-polarized state, yet the microscopic evolution between these limits remains unresolved. Here we report high-field specific heat measurements up to 24 T that reveal a distinct crossover at $μ_0H^*\approx$15 T, beyond which the perturbative Kitaev description breaks down. Above $H^*$, the characteristic six-fold angular modulation of the specific heat collapses and the excitation gap deviates from the predicted $H^3$ scaling. Meanwhile, the gap decreases with increasing field and the in-plane magnetization anisotropy persists up to $\sim$ 24 T, both in sharp contrast to a trivial spin-polarized state, indicating that KQSL signatures are preserved even at $\sim$ 90 % of magnetization saturation. These results reveal that the KQSL in $α$-RuCl$_3$ extends well beyond the perturbative window, persisting as a nonperturbative regime in which the Majorana and vison energy scales merge, before eventually giving way to spin polarization. This thermodynamic roadmap provides a basis for understanding how fractionalized phases evolve under strong magnetic fields.
summary: This work investigates how the Kitaev quantum spin liquid state in $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ behaves under very strong magnetic fields. By measuring specific heat up to 24 T, the researchers found that topological signatures, like angular modulations, persist far beyond the limits of simple theoretical models. This reveals a complex, nonperturbative high-field phase where the underlying fractionalized excitations remain active.
main_problem: The primary goal is to determine the fate of the Kitaev quantum spin liquid (KQSL) state in $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ when subjected to strong external magnetic fields, especially beyond the regime where simple perturbative theories apply.
main_result: KQSL signatures persist well beyond the perturbative window, indicating a nonperturbative regime where Majorana and vison energy scales merge, contrasting sharply with predictions for a simple spin-polarized state.
method: The study relies on high-field specific heat measurements ($C/T$) and in-plane magnetization measurements, analyzing the field and angle dependence of thermodynamic quantities.
model_or_system: The system is the layered honeycomb magnet $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$, which is investigated as a realization of the Kitaev quantum spin liquid (KQSL) model, featuring itinerant Majorana quasiparticles and gapped $Z_2$ fluxes (visons).
key_observables: Specific heat divided by temperature ($C/T$), in-plane magnetization anisotropy, and the extracted excitation gap ($\Delta$).
important_parameters: Magnetic field strength (up to 24 T), crossover field $H^* \approx 15$ T, and the temperature $T$.
main_assumptions: The analysis involves fitting $C/T$ data using activated forms to extract an effective gap, and the initial analysis relies on the perturbative Kitaev description.
figures_summary: Figures show the field-angle dependence of $C/T$ (revealing six-fold modulation at low fields), the evolution of the extracted gap $\Delta$ (showing non-monotonic behavior), and the persistence of magnetization anisotropy up to high fields.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the expected behavior in the perturbative regime (low fields), then identifying the breakdown point ($H^*$), and finally mapping the nonperturbative high-field regime by tracking the persistence of topological signatures.
why_interesting: The persistence of fractionalized excitations (Majorana/vison merging) in a nonperturbative, high-field regime provides crucial insight into the robustness of topological quantum matter under extreme conditions, relevant for understanding emergent quantum phases.
